key_insight: A multi-branch shell model shows that adding branching geometry to quasi-local triadic dynamics makes turbulent cascades more intermittent.
engineering_relevance: For reduced-order turbulence models and cascade-based closures, the result indicates that capturing intermittency may require both nonlinear interaction structure and scale-dependent branching of degrees of freedom.
method: Compared a multi-branch shell model against the standard Sabra shell model.
Measured intermittency using anomalous scaling exponents of energy-flux structure functions.
Analyzed multiplier statistics and large-deviation behavior to probe multiplicative cascade dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that branching enhances intermittency relative to the Sabra model, as evidenced by anomalous scaling exponents and supporting multiplier/large-deviation statistics.
watch_item: As a reduced model, the branching structure may not fully capture Navier–Stokes turbulence details, so direct quantitative transfer to real flows should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Intermittency in Shell Models of Turbulent Cascades: from Single-Branch to Multi-Branch
